title: Specialty Pharmacy Program Clinical Standard: Assessments, Adherence Outreach and Care Contacts
content:
## Standard

1. **Assessment interval.** Under the Specialty Pharmacy Program, a specialty pharmacist completes a clinical assessment at least once in every interval of the tier's assessment-interval calendar days. The time since assessment is the number of calendar days from the date of the latest completed clinical assessment contact on the enrollment through today. Where no assessment has yet been completed, it is counted from the activation date.
2. **Adherence outreach.** Where the tier runs adherence outreach, a member whose proportion of days covered falls below the tier's adherence threshold receives an adherence outreach contact.
3. **Recorded contacts.** Onboarding calls, refill reminders and injection training are recorded as care contacts, each with its outcome. Where the tier provides around-the-clock access, the care team is reachable around the clock.
4. **Enrollment status.** Care contacts are made only for enrollments that are active or on hold. The enrollment's status in the system record decides this.

## Status table

| Enrollment status | May a care contact be made? |
|---|---|
| active | Yes |
| on hold | Yes |
| referred, benefits verification or discharged | No |

## Elapsed days worked through (assumed dates, non-leap year)

| Latest completed clinical assessment | Today | Calendar days elapsed |
|---|---|---|
| January 10 | April 10 | 90 |
| none; activated February 1 | March 3 | 30 |

On a tier with a 90-day interval, 90 days elapsed means the assessment interval has been reached.

## Adherence cases (assumed tier that runs outreach with an 80% threshold)

- A proportion of days covered of 0.72 is below the threshold, so an adherence outreach contact is made.
- A proportion of 0.80 is not below the threshold.
